p0.title: Night decree: shame is revoked
p0.intro: The chapter waives the obligation to apologize for one's identity. Moral panic has no veto power.
p0.b0: We, the self-appointed Chapter of Zakon Czarnego Kału, after consulting one skeleton and the last functioning cell of common sense, declare an end to penance for other people’s prejudices.
p0.b1: § 1. Gay pride is not a request for approval. A boy can love a boy without the seal of approval of the Committee on Other People's Bedrooms.
p0.b2: § 2. Anyone who cries about the collapse of civilization at the sight of two men holding hands should check whether their civilization was built from soggy cardboard.
p0.b3: § 3. The Order demands loyalty to its principles: consent, freedom and mutual respect. No title within the Order exempts anyone from thinking.
p0.b4: The decree bears the Black Seal. Appeals may be addressed to the Grand Chancellor of None of Your Business.
p1.title: Applied necromancy: this dead dogma will not rise
p1.intro: Reviving a skeleton is a piece of cake. Restoring meaning to dead prejudices is beyond the Order's ability.
p1.b0: In our fictional crypt, the necromancer resurrects memes, jokes and the courage to be yourself. No budget was allocated, however, to reviving the idea that someone else’s orientation is a matter for a public tribunal.
p1.b1: A skeleton has one advantage over a hypocrite: at least it does not pretend to have a moral backbone. The bar is low, but the Chapter records every success.
p1.b2: Being gay is not a curse. Believing that your own fear entitles you to control someone else’s love is the curse. We do not cast that spell.
p1.b3: The rule of Zakon Czarnego Kału is simple: resurrect humour, bury contempt and respect consent. If a ritual requires stripping someone of their dignity, the ritual belongs in the bin.
p2.title: Decree No. 001: on the establishment of solemnity
p2.intro: The Chapter decides that from now on, trivial matters will be considered with full ceremony.
p2.b0: On the date of this decree, solemnity is hereby established as the official setting for every activity of the Order. The activities themselves remain optional, with a preference for a sensible lack of sense.
p2.b1: § 1. Each meeting may be considered a meeting of the Chapter if at least one person says: "Okay, listen."
p2.b2: § 2. The minutes are drawn up by the person who first asks whether anyone is writing them down. The lack of minutes does not invalidate a successful meeting.
p2.b3: § 3. Titles shall be bestowed in moderation. Permitted offices include Grand Keeper of the Charger and Commissioner for Things That Were Only Supposed to Take a Minute.
p2.b4: The decree takes effect immediately upon being read. You may appeal, but you will need a better joke.
p3.title: In the beginning there was a sketch. And the arrow.
p3.intro: Every legend needs a beginning. Ours was one WhatsApp photo.
p3.b0: There was no competition, committee or forty-slide strategy presentation. There was a friend’s hand-drawn sketch: a symbol, an arrow, a few wisps and three letters. ZCK.
p3.b1: This sketch became the starting point for our emblem. We retained its most important motifs: a stylized form, a diagonal arrow and four streaks. We added a setting that treats the theme with ceremonial exaggeration.
p3.b2: That is the Order’s entire method: take a shared joke, give it a language of its own and see how far imagination can carry it.
p3.b3: This entry opens the chronicle. Further events are in the hands of life and the group chat.
p4.title: A short treatise on not taking yourself too seriously
p4.intro: Can an initiative without a goal have a direction? Yes. It is indicated by an arrow in the coat of arms.
p4.b0: You have to take many things seriously in life. That's why it's useful to have a place where you can put your formal tone aside for a moment and then immediately put it back on - just for fun.
p4.b1: A sense of perspective does not mean caring about nothing. It means recognizing that the title of Grand Chancellor of Unimportant Affairs makes no one more important than the person who simply came to hang out.
p4.b2: Our rule is simple: a good joke leaves room for everyone at the table. If someone doesn't feel like laughing, there's no need to appoint an investigation committee.
p4.b3: And if someone asks what all this is for? You can say: to have something to look back on. That is a perfectly serious reason.
